newsitem.title: USA: Atmel shares jump after better-than-expected earnings.
newsitem.headline: Atmel shares jump after better-than-expected earnings.

text.p: Atmel Corp. shares surged as much as 12 percent Friday after executives of the computer chipmaker said they expect new products to bolster earnings in the second half of the year.
Shares of Atmel, based in San Jose, Calif., jumped $2.875 to $31.375 in early afternoon Nasdaq trading. Earlier, the shares traded as high as $31.875.

After the market closed Thursday, Atmel, which makes specialised processors and memory chips, reported that second-quarter earnings dropped to $27.4 million from $50.3 million in the comparable 1996 period.
However, company executives told analysts they expect strong orders in the third quarter.
"The company is feeling very bullish about its new products and prospects for the second half of the year," said Scott Randall, a semiconductor analyst at investment bank SoundView Financial.

The company recently began shipping a new, more efficient flash-memory chip, an electronic component used in computers and consumer electronics, and a new microcontroller, a specialised chip for performing the fundamental functions of computers.
Atmel also said it has $101 of orders for products for every $100 worth of products it ships.
Atmel, like other semiconductor companies, has been facing a plunge in prices for commodity chips. The new products could help Atmel increase its prices, analysts said.
"We believe that fundamentals are improving for Atmel and that bookings will continue to improve," Greg Mischou, analyst at Alex. Brown & Sons Inc., wrote in a research report released Friday.
